long_biography.plain_text:
Banded protectors and slow-recovery foam plugs were central to the industrial-safety manufacturer Howard S. Leight established in the early 1970s. His exposure to the field predated that venture: Leight's father had supplied earplugs to shipyard workers during the First World War. Bacou acquired substantially all assets of Howard Leight Industries in 1998, while a separate supplier briefly retained Leight and other former executives as shareholders.

The product marque subsequently passed from Bacou-Dalloz to Sperian Protection and finally Honeywell, leaving its factories, intellectual property and sales operations outside the founder's holdings. Leight instead pursued real-estate investments, among them the estate developed as Malibu Rocky Oaks. Howard Leight Jr. cultivated and ran the winery there. The present allocation of the elder Leight's private portfolio is not known.

uncertainties.detail: Howard Leight and Howard Leight Jr. appear together in reporting on Malibu Rocky Oaks. Forbes and the Los Angeles Business Journal assign the original hearing-protection company and property purchase to the father and the winery's cultivation and operations to the son; the dossier preserves that distinction.

Leight sold substantially all operating assets to Bacou in 1998. The brand later passed through Bacou-Dalloz and Sperian to Honeywell. Honeywell's brand, products, factories, patents and other operating assets are not treated as Leight's current personal property.

Howard Leight Enterprises was a separately formed raw-material supplier owned by Leight and other former executives after the sale. Public records describe a five-year supply arrangement but do not establish it as a current holding, so it is not presented as an ongoing business.
